correctness.rationale: For q>=2 the Burnside necklace count N_q(d)=q^d/d+O(d q^{d/2}) makes the ordinary isomorphism-class generating function an isolated simple pole at z=1/q times a nonzero analytic factor on |z|<q^-1/2. Multiplicity marking yields geometric limits and exponential coefficient errors for every bounded collection of necklace counts. A separate disjoint-block argument bounds the number of necklaces avoiding T occurrences of any fixed long colour block by O(d^T beta^d), beta<q; thus missing a T-rich cycle is exponentially unlikely. Bounded-degree Hanf locality reduces each fixed first-order sentence to finite capped necklace multiplicities once all long-path local types are saturated. Therefore all limits are rational and convergence is exponentially fast. The q=1 paragraph uses classical partition-number ratio asymptotics, explicitly credited as old. The checker reproduces rotation-orbit necklace counts, exact coefficients, multiplicity markers and fixed-point probabilities using integer/fraction arithmetic; finite checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The inspected recent source studies unary-function model-counting complexity and a labelled automorphism-marking reduction, not the unlabelled FO distribution. Albert–Bouvel–Féray explicitly cite the uncoloured unlabelled zero-one law, which is excluded from claimed novelty. Burris–Yeats cite Compton’s ratio-test criterion for a zero-one law, not an explicit q>=2 rational/exponentially convergent first-order law. Accessible prior research on labelled coloured permutations studies a different probability measure and the distribution of automorphism groups. A direct collection of source/claim/alias/parameter searches found related necklace or unary-algebra records but no matching theorem. Historic priority remains subject to the specific risk listed.

value.rationale: The fully motivated question asks for all first-order probabilities under the genuinely unlabelled sampling measure in a natural unary-bijection model class, directly relevant to current unlabeled model-counting research. The result completely classifies those limits as rational, proves a nontrivial uniform exponential rate for each fixed sentence, and identifies the structurally important fixed-colour transition from the previously known q=1 zero-one regime to a nontrivial q>=2 law. The proof needs a pattern-rich necklace lemma, singularity analysis and Hanf locality, not merely small-n recomputation or a renamed general theorem. No theorem for unrelated subclasses is inflated into a new contribution.
